questions.question: Before a trip, how can you make sure air flows to all trailers?

options.text: Check for moving air inside each trailer.
Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
Feel for air at the front shut-off valve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen for air at the rear shut-off valve.
questions.explanation: Before a trip, check that air reaches all trailers. Let air pressure build up. Send air to the emergency and service lines. Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If you hear air escaping from these valves, air is reaching the entire vehicle.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor attached to two trailers

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a trailer. Drivers must be careful when operating a bobtail tractor.

questions.question: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air supply leaks away, what happens?

options.text: The trailer will not have brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer will not have brakes.
questions.explanation: Older trailers do not have spring brakes. If the air tank loses pressure, there are no working brakes. The trailer's wheels will turn freely with no braking power.

questions.question: When braking with ABS, what should you do?

options.text: Push the brake pedal harder than usual.
Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
Push the brake pedal more lightly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal as you normally would.
questions.explanation: When using ABS, apply your brakes the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: How should you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Release air with the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air with the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully. Turn off the engine. Press the brake pedal several times to release air from the system. When the pressure drops to an unsafe level, the tractor protection valve should move to its emergency position.

questions.question: If an air supply control is in its emergency position, what happens?

options.text: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
The air supply to the trailer will increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer emergency brakes will be applied.
questions.explanation: When an air supply control is in its emergency position, the air supply stops and the trailer emergency brakes are applied.

questions.question: After completing a pre-trip inspection, you should ensure that the:
questions.explanation: Before a trip, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves and listen for escaping air to confirm all brakes work. Close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: If you push the tractor air supply control and your trailer's spring brakes do not release, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the engine off and on again.

questions.explanation: All equipment must work properly before a trip. If the spring brakes do not release when you push the tractor air supply control, check that the air line connections are properly attached and sealed.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), how should brakes be applied?

options.text: In the same way as they would be in a vehicle without ABS.
As the vehicle is placed in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the same way as they would be in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: When driving a vehicle with ABS, brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.question: Keeping cargo centered on a rig can:
questions.explanation: A rollover is more likely if cargo is unevenly loaded. Keep the load centered on the rig to help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: Which trailer is most likely to roll over if the driver turns too quickly?
questions.explanation: When turning, steer slowly and smoothly. Quick turns while pulling trailers are dangerous. The last trailer is most likely to roll over.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?
questions.explanation: Push in the control to send air to the trailer. Pull it out to stop the air supply and activate emergency brakes.

questions.question: How much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?

options.text: A maximum of two inches of space

questions.explanation: Before driving, inspect all couplings. There should be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.

questions.question: When backing up to couple a trailer, where should the tractor be positioned?

options.text: Directly in front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Directly in front of the trailer.
questions.explanation: Position the tractor directly in front of the trailer when backing up. Backing at an angle can cause the trailer to move and break the landing gear.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, what should the driver do?

options.text: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
Can straighten the trailer with the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not apply the trailer hand brake.
questions.explanation: If a trailer jackknifes, release the brakes to let the wheels grip the road again. Do not use the trailer hand brake. Braking is what caused the wheels to lock in the first place.

questions.question: An empty combination vehicle with stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have:
questions.explanation: An empty vehicle stops more slowly than a loaded one. With less weight, the stiff springs and strong brakes have lower traction.

questions.question: When pulling a trailer, the air supply control lever should be in which position?
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. Set the air supply control to "normal" when pulling a trailer.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor without a semi-trailer. Bobtail tractors are hard to operate and require caution.

questions.question: All trailers made after what year must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: How do you test the trailer service brakes?
questions.explanation: To test the trailer service brakes, check that the air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control. You should feel the brakes activate if they work properly.
